Log-ratio transforms of compositions

Source: R/tph.R
clrilr.Rd

Element shares from portable X-ray fluorescence of bone or soil, or any parts of a whole, live on the simplex: they sum to one, and ordinary statistics on the raw shares mislead. The centred log-ratio ("clr") takes each part's log over the geometric mean of its row; the isometric log-ratio ("ilr", Egozcue et al. 2003) gives d - 1 coordinates in an orthonormal basis (the default pivot basis: coordinate i contrasts the first i parts with part i + 1), on which the usual methods apply. Each row is closed to sum 1 after ps is added to every part, so that a part below the detection limit (0) has a log.

Usage

clrilr(x, type = "clr", ps = 1e-06)

Arguments

x

The compositions: a numeric matrix or data frame of numbers from 0, one row per sample and one column per part, at least two parts.

type

"clr" or "ilr".

ps

The pseudocount added to every part: one number from 0.

Value

A matrix with one row per sample: d columns named as the parts ("clr"), or d - 1 columns ilr1, ilr2, ... ("ilr").

References

Aitchison, J. (1986). The Statistical Analysis of Compositional Data. Chapman and Hall. doi:10.1007/978-94-009-4109-0

Egozcue, J. J., Pawlowsky-Glahn, V., Mateu-Figueras, G. and Barcelo-Vidal, C. (2003). Isometric logratio transformations for compositional data analysis. Mathematical Geology, 35(3), 279-300. doi:10.1023/A:1023818214614

Examples

x <- rbind(c(Ca = 60, P = 25, Fe = 10, Zn = 5),
           c(Ca = 80, P = 12, Fe = 6, Zn = 2))
clrilr(x)
#>            Ca         P         Fe        Zn
#> [1,] 1.288034 0.4125649 -0.5037257 -1.196873
#> [2,] 2.044066 0.1469466 -0.5462005 -1.644812
clrilr(x, "ilr")
#>           ilr1     ilr2     ilr3
#> [1,] 0.6190499 1.105557 1.382030
#> [2,] 1.3414664 1.340448 1.899266
